transfer.stem: Which report follows all three design notes?
transfer.passage:
Design notes for our trail display
Our club made a display to explain a new walking trail. We folded a square sheet into a triangle for a sign. For another part, the instructions asked us to draw a rectangle twice as long as it was wide. They specified a relationship between the sides, not one fixed size.
We drew a line from a label to the matching picture. A ladybird drawing showed one black spot on each of its two wing cases. We checked each side separately: putting two on one side and none on the other would not match the note. The drawing did not describe every kind of ladybird.
A sports jacket in the display had a long yellow stripe along one sleeve and a separate round yellow badge on its chest. The chest badge was not the sleeve stripe.
Before adding details to a sketch, we drew its outline. We also used sandpaper to smooth a sharp edge on a wooden display piece. A final card described a bridge whose curved roof was its main feature. We kept the shape of the roof and its importance together when writing the report.

options.text: The rectangle’s length was twice its width; each wing case had one black spot; the yellow stripe ran along the sleeve.
The rectangle’s width was twice its length; each wing case had one black spot; the yellow stripe ran along the sleeve.
The rectangle’s length was twice its width; two black spots were on one wing case and none on the other; the yellow stripe ran along the sleeve.
The rectangle’s length was twice its width; each wing case had one black spot; the yellow stripe was the round chest badge.
